transcript.content: Hello, welcome. Can you tell me what brings you in today?

Well… I guess I just haven’t been feeling like myself lately. It’s probably not as bad as it sounds, but I’ve been getting really quiet, not talking to people much. Kind of flat, I guess.

Even at work, getting started on my cleaning route feels… heavier than it should, like I’m pushing a loaded cart uphill. I thought maybe I should come in before it gets worse, if that makes sense.
How long have you been feeling this way?

It’s been… a while, I guess. Maybe about a year and five months, if I’m counting right. It started building after I had to leave my old apartment and neighborhood. I didn’t think it would affect me that much, but… yeah, that’s around when it began.
Have you noticed that things you used to enjoy, like hobbies or spending time with friends, don’t interest you as much anymore?

Yeah… I guess I have noticed that. I don’t want to make it sound dramatic, but things just don’t really pull me in the way they used to.

Like, I used to look forward to fishing on Saturdays, or doing crosswords with my coffee. Even at work, I liked showing the younger guys little tricks for stripping a floor right. Now I mostly just… let those things sit. They don’t really give me much back, if that makes sense.
Have you noticed any changes in your energy levels or do you feel more tired than usual, even when you haven’t been doing much?

Yeah… I mean, I don’t want to overstate it, but I have been more worn out than I think I should be.

Even if I sleep through the night, by the time I get to the building my arms and legs can feel kind of heavy. And little things, like hauling trash bags, seem to take more out of me than they used to. I still get through it, mostly, but… it’s harder than I’d like to admit. Is that the kind of thing you mean?
Have you found yourself feeling more down on yourself lately, like you’re not worth much or that you’re letting people down, even if you’re doing your best?

Yeah… I suppose I do, more than I’d like to admit.

I try not to sit around feeling sorry for myself, but I keep thinking I kind of failed everybody when I lost my old place… like I should’ve kept things together better than I did. And then it spills over into other things too. If the church pantry is short on supplies, or if I miss a hallway at work, I start thinking, “Well, that’s on me,” even when maybe it isn’t all mine to carry.

I know that probably doesn’t sound very logical… but that’s where my mind goes. Is that what you mean?
Have there been times when you felt unusually high, overly energetic, or so good that you didn’t feel like you needed much sleep, even if just for a few days?

I don’t think so… not really like that.

I mean, I’ve had days where I’m in a better mood or I get a little more done than usual, but not where I felt, you know, on top of the world or like I didn’t need sleep for days. If anything, I usually still want the sleep.

Is that what you’re asking?
Have you noticed yourself moving more slowly than usual, or maybe feeling restless and unable to sit still, like your body is matching how your mind is feeling?

I’m not sure I’ve noticed that, exactly.

I mean, I move slower sometimes when I’m tired, I guess, but I don’t know if it’s more than anybody else would. And I don’t think I’m pacing around or unable to sit still, not in a way I’ve really paid attention to.

Maybe I should watch for it more… but right now I don’t think I could say yes to that. Is that okay?
Have you had days when you feel down or lose interest in things almost all day, nearly every day, for a period of time?

Yeah… I think that does happen. I don’t want to make it sound worse than it is, but there are stretches where I just don’t really feel much pull toward things.

Like, I used to look forward to fishing on Saturdays, or sitting with coffee and doing crosswords. Even at work, I used to kind of enjoy showing the younger guys little tricks for stripping a floor the right way. Lately I mostly just… let those things sit. They don’t give me much back, if that makes sense.

I still try to keep going, but the interest part, it’s been pretty low. Is that the kind of thing you mean?
Have you ever had a period before this one where you felt this way for several weeks or more, where it seemed like you were just going through the motions most days?

I’m not really sure… I mean, I’ve had rough patches before, sure, but I don’t know if I could honestly say it was several weeks or more in the same way.

Sometimes life just feels kind of routine, you know—work, home, sleep, do it again. But whether that was me being “down” like this, or just tired and getting older, I’m not positive.

I don’t want to overstate it. I guess I’d say maybe, but I’d have to think on it a little more. Is that an okay answer?
Can you think back and tell me if there was ever a time before this current period when you felt down or lost interest in things nearly every day for at least two weeks in a row?

Yeah… I’m trying to think back. I don’t know if I can pin down another time before this one where it was clearly two weeks straight, nearly every day.

What I can say is this current stretch has that feeling — like I used to look forward to things, fishing on Saturdays, or coffee and a crossword, even showing the younger guys at work how to strip a floor right. And now I mostly just let those things sit because they don’t really give me anything back.

Before this, maybe I had little spells like that, but I’m not sure I’d want to say it was that long unless I knew. I don’t want to answer wrong. Does that make sense?
Can you think back and tell me if there was ever a time before this current period when you felt down or lost interest in things nearly every day for at least two weeks in a row?

I wish I could give you a cleaner yes or no, but I’m not sure.

Before this current stretch, I know I had times where I felt worn down or kind of flat, but I don’t remember clearly that it was nearly every day for two full weeks. I don’t want to say yes just to be agreeable if I can’t really back it up.

So… maybe there were shorter patches, but I can’t honestly point to one before this and say, “yes, that was at least two weeks.” Is that alright?
Can you remember having more than one time in your life when you felt down or lost interest in things nearly every day for at least two weeks?

I don’t think I can say more than one, no… not clearly.

I mean, I’ve had times in life where I wasn’t exactly cheerful, but when you say nearly every day for two weeks, that’s pretty specific. I can’t honestly remember multiple times like that.

So I’d say… not that I can remember. I hope that’s a useful answer.
Looking back, can you recall if there was ever a time before this current period when you felt down or lost interest in things for at least two weeks straight?

I’m not totally sure before this current one, if I’m being honest. I don’t want to make it sound worse than it was.

Right now, though, yeah… it’s like the things I used to look forward to don’t really pull me anymore. Fishing on Saturdays, coffee and a crossword, even showing the younger guys at work little tricks for stripping a floor — I used to get something out of that. Lately I mostly just let those things sit, because they don’t give me much back.

But before this period… I can’t clearly say there was another full two weeks like that. Is that the kind of thing you’re asking?
Can you remember a time before this current period when you had a clear improvement in your mood and functioning for at least two months, where you were back to feeling more like your usual self?

I’m not sure I can point to a clear stretch like that, honestly.

I mean, there have been days or maybe little stretches where I functioned better, went to work, kept up more, and I probably seemed more like myself. But “at least two months” where I was clearly improved and back to usual… I don’t want to say yes if I can’t really remember it that cleanly.

So I guess my answer is, I’m not sure. I don’t have a specific time in mind that fits that. Does that make sense?

Looking back, can you recall if there was ever a time before this current period when you had a clear improvement in your mood and functioning for at least two months, where you were back to feeling more like your usual self?

I know I kind of answered that already, but… no, I don’t think I can really pick out a solid two-month stretch like that before this.

There might’ve been times I was doing a bit better, keeping up with things more, and I don’t want to make it sound like it was all bad. But “back to my usual self” for a couple months straight… I can’t honestly say I remember that clearly.

Sorry, I know that’s not the most exact answer.
